texts: waiting in the market
Write a doha about a vendor who sits patiently in the market all day, never pushing or pleading for customers, trusting that what is meant to come to him will arrive in its own time.
I've been sitting at my stall in the market for three weeks with hardly any sales, and my father keeps telling me to hold steady and let things come.
doha: be calm in the market, your day will come
In the market's hurry, one still voice waits, knowing the hour that is his will find him.
Do not pull at the hour; it opens by itself when the time is right.
I've applied to forty jobs and heard nothing, and my mother just says be calm, your turn will come.
wait for the right time

Please write a doha about a restless person who wants everything immediately, and the gentle reminder that all things happen at their own pace, so that haste only brings sorrow and calm waiting brings peace.
doha on being patient pls

Compose a doha about a lamp that burns steadily through the long night without hurrying the dawn, a picture of a patient person who endures dark times quietly, knowing that morning comes in its own time.
lamp, waiting for dawn
Since my surgery I've been sitting at home recovering, lighting a small lamp each evening, waiting for the day I can walk freely again.
The lamp does not beg the dawn to hurry; it burns, and the dawn comes.
doha: a lamp waiting out the night, patience
doha: lamp on a boat, waiting for the shore
Write a doha about a small lamp on a boat that burns calmly while the boat drifts across the dark waters, with no hurry to reach the shore, trusting that the crossing will end when it is meant to.
I'm in the middle of a long wait for a visa and feel like I'm drifting at night in a boat with only a small lamp, not knowing when we'll reach land.
boat, lamp, calm waiting
Lamp on the boat, shore still far; yet the lamp burns on, and the shore comes in due time.
My sister is going through a very slow recovery and keeps getting frustrated, and I'd like to send her something to remind her that healing takes its own time.
Compose a doha for someone who wants quick results but is learning that most good things take time, reminding them that rushing spoils what patience would have allowed to be completed properly.
doha about not rushing things
slow and steady
Hurry is a restless fever; calm waiting is the quiet that lets all things arrive.
The fisherman waits, and the fish arrives not by his will but in its own time.
doha: fisherman waiting for a catch, patience
Write a doha about a fisherman who sits quietly all day without complaint, never pulling or pushing, who knows the fish will come when it is time and not a moment before, and so is at peace.
fish, patient wait
My grandfather spends whole mornings at the lake waiting for a single fish, and says that's where he learned never to be in a hurry about anything.
moth, waiting
doha: a moth waiting patiently till night
My daughter sat by the window all day waiting for the evening so the moths would come, and didn't complain once.
Compose a doha about a moth that waits calmly through the long day for the evening to come, never fretting, a picture of a patient person who trusts that the right hour arrives on its own.
The moth waits out the day in quiet, for night will come without being summoned.
My grandfather has been rubbing sandalwood and turning his prayer beads every dawn for forty years, and he says he has never once been in a hurry to get anywhere.
beads, sandalwood, patience

Write a doha about a devotee who turns his prayer beads and rubs sandalwood paste every morning without hurrying, understanding that quiet repetition over many years brings its own reward, which cannot be forced.
Bead by bead, day by day, the sandalwood is ground; so is steadiness made.
doha: prayer beads and sandalwood, slow and steady
Compose a doha about a moth sitting quietly on a boat at night while the vessel drifts slowly toward the far shore, a picture of calm waiting that trusts the journey will end in its own time.
doha: moth on a boat, calmly waiting
I'm stuck waiting for results after months of interviews and I feel like a moth resting on the edge of a slow boat: nothing to do but be still and let it move.
The moth rests on the boat that drifts; neither hurries, and both arrive.
moth, boat, patience
Write a doha about a seller in the market who remains calm and kind even when no one buys anything, trusting that every customer comes at the right hour and that hurrying them would spoil it all.
The market's tide goes out and comes in; the patient man sits, and the tide returns.
market, patience
My cousin's business has been very slow at the market for months and he hasn't panicked, he just keeps opening his stall at the same time every day.
doha: be patient in the market, the buyers will come
Compose a doha about a lamp that does not hurry the dawn, burning steadily while waiting for morning, and about the quiet person who, like the lamp, waits through dark times without panicking.
My brother is in hospital and we have no choice but to wait for his test results, and I keep a small lamp lit for him each night.
lamp, waiting
doha: lamp burning through a long wait
The lamp burns in the long night and asks nothing of the hour.

Write a doha about a sandalwood tree that grows slowly for many years before its fragrance matures, and how the patient person, like the tree, must give time its due and not demand the results of years in a day.
The sandalwood tree is in no hurry; its fragrance deepens with the years.
sandalwood tree, slow growth
doha: sandalwood tree grows slowly, be patient
My grandfather planted a sandalwood tree when I was born and says it will be fully ready only when I am forty, and that nothing good should be rushed.
The hour has its own time to come; to demand it earlier is only noise.

Write a doha about the wisdom of waiting calmly for the right moment, letting events unfold without forcing them, because everything in life has its own pace, and trying to hurry it only causes needless suffering.
doha on patience pls
calm waiting
I've been waiting for my exam results for six weeks and my grandmother keeps telling me nothing happens before its hour.
My uncle is a potter who spends hours grinding sandalwood paste to rub on his pots, never rushing, and says good work cannot be hurried.
Compose a doha about a potter who patiently shapes his clay and slowly grinds sandalwood for a finishing touch, never hurrying, because good things take time and cannot be forced into being.
potter, sandalwood, patience
Slowly the clay is shaped, slowly the sandalwood is ground, and haste makes both unfit.
doha: potter + sandalwood, slow work wins
doha: sandalwood takes time to give its fragrance
sandalwood, slow fragrance
Sandalwood does not hurry its scent; time alone makes it sweet.
Write a doha about sandalwood that must be ground slowly on a stone before it releases its fragrance, a picture of how patience and slow effort bring out the best in anything worth having.
I'm learning classical music and my teacher told me, gently, that it takes years of daily practice, like rubbing sandalwood on stone, before the sweetness comes.

Write a doha about a person who turns prayer beads slowly and calmly every day, never impatient for results, understanding that spiritual growth takes years and cannot be forced, so each bead is its own peace.
I started meditating three months ago and still feel nothing special, but my grandmother, sitting with her prayer beads, says just keep going; it comes in its own time.
prayer beads, patience
doha: slowly turning prayer beads, no hurry
One bead at a time, with no hurry for the last; so the patient heart is made.
Last night I sat on the porch waiting for my daughter's flight to land, and a single moth sat beside me the whole time, equally still.
doha: a moth sitting still, waiting
The moth sits still in the evening hush, for what it waits for will surely come.
Compose a doha about a moth resting calmly at dusk, not fluttering or fretting, trusting that what it awaits will come when its moment arrives, and teaching the restless heart to be still.
moth, stillness
Bead by bead the rope descends the well, and the water rises in its own hour.
My grandmother draws water from the well every dawn, slowly, with her prayer beads tucked in her sash, and never once complains of the wait.
Write a doha about a patient devotee who turns prayer beads by the well each morning and waits for the bucket to rise, knowing that the deepest things come slowly and cannot be drawn up faster.
well, beads, patience
doha: prayer beads by the well, slow and calm

Compose a doha about sandalwood that takes decades to mature and release its scent, and about the person who has learned to trust the slow pace of life and does not demand its rewards before their time.
I've been trying to get my small business off the ground for three years with little reward, and my dad, who works with sandalwood, tells me good things always take a long while.
sandalwood, slow reward
doha: sandalwood and patience, good things take time
Sandalwood takes its years to mature, and the patient man takes his.

Please write a doha about a person who has been waiting a long time for something important, who has learned to rest in the waiting instead of fighting it, and who trusts that every thing arrives at its appointed time.
We have been trying for a baby for four years, and my mother-in-law keeps saying in her gentle way that these things come in their own time.
doha for when you have to wait a long time
Wait, O restless heart, for the hour is not late; it is only not yet.
waiting calmly
Write a doha about a person who lowers a bucket into a deep well by lamplight, content to wait for it to fill without hurry, a picture of the patient mind that lets things come slowly and surely.
well, lamp, patience
Our village waits for rain every summer, and each evening my grandfather lights a lamp by the well, saying the water will come when it is meant to.
By the lamp at the well, he waits, and the water rises in its own time.
doha: lamp + well, patiently waiting
The market hurries and shouts; the patient merchant sits, and his hour finds him.
doha: be patient at the market, sales will come

Compose a doha about a trader in the noisy market who sits quietly while the others push and shout, trusting that his own customers will arrive at their own pace, and that calm brings better fortune than haste.
market, calm waiting
My friend just started a stall at the market, and everyone else is rushing around, but he just sits there patiently and his sales are slowly picking up.
The well fills drop by drop, in no hurry, and in the end overflows.
My father has dug at our well for weeks and it's still dry, but he says water comes when the ground is ready, and not a day sooner.
Write a doha about a man who digs a well patiently day after day, never discouraged by the dry earth, and who trusts that water will come in its own time to reward calm and constant effort.
doha: digging a well takes time, be patient
well, slow reward
I'd like a doha about how the person who is calm in waiting has already won half the battle, because patience removes the pain of time, and what is meant to come will arrive without any struggle.
He who waits without fret lets the hour come as a friend.
doha about being calm while waiting
I've been waiting in a hospital for six hours for news about my dad, and I want something to calm me down.
stay calm, wait
My daughter wants to learn the violin overnight, but I've told her it's like sandalwood, which needs time to reveal its fragrance.
sandalwood, patience
Sandalwood, ground slowly, yields its fragrance; haste only breaks the stone.

Compose a doha about sandalwood that gives its fragrance only to the patient hand that grinds it slowly, teaching that good things reveal themselves with time and quiet persistence, not with force or haste.
doha: sandalwood & slow time

Write a doha about a gardener who waters a young tree every day and does not expect fruit before the season, trusting that everything has its time, and that no amount of watering can hurry the ripening.
doha: water the tree daily but fruit comes in season
tree, fruit in season
The tree bears fruit in its season; no hurry of the gardener can hasten it.
I've been working hard on a project for two years and nothing has come of it yet, and my dad keeps saying you can't force the tree to fruit.
Fish rise in their own hour, and sandalwood sweetens with its years; hurry spoils them both.
fish, sandalwood, patience
Compose a doha about a patient fisherman who rubs sandalwood on his hands and waits for the fish, understanding that every good thing arrives at its own time and cannot be hurried by wishing.
My grandfather, a fisherman, applies sandalwood paste on his forehead every morning and waits patiently for his catch, never in a rush, and says that's the whole secret of life.
doha: fish and sandalwood, waiting calmly
doha: sandalwood is slow to mature, like good things
Time grinds the sandalwood, and its fragrance is time's reward.
My grandmother's sandalwood box has taken years to take on its scent, and she says that's how everything worthwhile happens.
sandalwood, slow time
Compose a doha about the way sandalwood takes years to gain its fragrance, and how a patient person, like sandalwood, grows into goodness slowly over a long time, rewarded at last by sweetness.
The potter waits for the clay to dry, the well waits for the rain; time shapes both.
doha: potter drying clay, well filling up, both need patience
My father the potter waits days for his clay to dry in the sun, and refills the well slowly from the stream, and says I'm too impatient for anything.
Write a doha about a potter who waits patiently for his clay to dry and for the well to fill, understanding that good work and good results come in their own time, and cannot be rushed by wishing.
potter, well, wait
Bead by bead the boat moves on; hurry cannot hasten the shore.
Compose a doha about a pilgrim in a slow boat who turns prayer beads calmly, never fretting about when the shore will come, because he knows the journey ends exactly when it should.
boat, beads, calm
We were stuck on the ferry for two hours, and my grandfather just quietly turned his prayer beads, saying we'd arrive when we arrive.
doha: slow boat and prayer beads, patience
calm endurance

Write a doha about the quiet strength of patience, how the one who can wait without anger or complaint always finds that the right time brings what he needs, while the impatient exhaust themselves in vain.
Calm endurance is the quiet strength that outlasts every trial.
I've been doing physiotherapy for months and progress is slow, and the therapist told me that my body has its own timetable.
doha pls on staying calm while waiting
doha: prayer beads and patience
I've been chanting every morning with my grandmother's prayer beads for a year and still nothing amazing has happened, but she says to keep going calmly.
Write a doha about a devotee who turns prayer beads each morning without expecting miracles, knowing that growth is slow and that the quiet repetition of years will bring peace in its own time.
Bead after patient bead, and the heart grows quiet.
beads, slow devotion
well, waiting for water
Compose a doha about a person waiting by a dry well for the rains, never losing hope, since the water that fills the well comes in its own season and is not made to hurry by anyone's complaints.
Our well went dry last summer, and my father just waits and says we shouldn't complain, the water will return when it's ready.
doha: well filling slowly, be patient
The well waits for the rain, not asking when, and in time it is full.
market, calm waiting
My uncle's stall at the market has been empty for hours, and he's just sitting there peacefully with a cup of tea, saying customers always come.
The patient seller in the market's rush sits like a rock in a river, and the crowds find him.

Write a doha about a seller at the market who waits calmly for customers, neither pleading nor losing heart, trusting that those who are meant to come will arrive, and the day will bring what it brings.
doha: be patient at the market, customers will come
lamp, tree, patience
Compose a doha about a lamp placed beneath a young tree that waits patiently for the tree to grow, showing that the best things take years and cannot be hurried by wishing or worrying.
Lamp beneath the sapling, and the night is long; the tree grows in the dark, slowly and surely.
doha: lamp and tree, slow growth
My grandfather lights a small lamp under the young tree he planted, and says it will take twenty years to give fruit, and he's perfectly content to wait.

Write a doha about a fish who swims through the water without hurry, for the current brings what it must at the right moment, a picture of the patient soul who trusts that things arrive in their own time.
The fish does not hasten the tide, and the tide brings it home.
I just started fishing with my father and I keep getting frustrated that nothing bites, and he keeps telling me that fish come when they come.
fish, calm waiting
doha: fishing teaches patience
I've been staring at the clock for hours waiting for a phone call, and a moth sitting calmly on the wall next to me suddenly made me feel foolish for being so anxious.
The moth rests through the day, content, for night will come when it will come.
doha: moth waiting for night, patience
Compose a doha about a moth resting through the daylight without agitation, knowing that its time to fly arrives with the evening, and teaching the anxious heart to wait calmly for its own hour.
moth, calm waiting
doha: potter planting a tree, slow growth
potter, tree, waiting
My grandfather is a potter, and he plants a tree each year knowing that he might never sit in its shade, saying that's what patience looks like.
The potter shapes clay in a day; the tree he plants will take its years, and he waits in peace.

Compose a doha about a potter who plants a tree beside his workshop and calmly accepts that it will grow in its own time, understanding that some things, unlike clay, cannot be shaped by hands, but only waited for.
doha about waiting for good things
My sister has been waiting for her visa for fourteen months and she's holding up better than I would.
waiting calmly
The hour that is yours will come; it cannot go to anyone else.

Please write a doha about the peace that comes from accepting that some things take a long time, about how worry never made anything arrive sooner, and how a calm heart passes the waiting hours more easily.
Beads for the hours, sandalwood for the years; the patient heart needs both and hurries neither.
Compose a doha about a devotee who patiently turns prayer beads and rubs sandalwood each dawn, in no hurry for results, trusting that the quiet work of the years will bring all that is needed.
doha: prayer beads and sandalwood, take your time
beads, sandalwood, calm
My grandmother does the same morning routine with her prayer beads and sandalwood every day, never rushing, and I've never seen her anxious about anything.
We have been waiting at the river bank for the boat for hours, and the old man next to me was calmly drawing water from the well, saying it would come when it came.
doha: boat and well, waiting patiently

Write a doha about a traveler who waits patiently at the well for the boat to arrive, neither complaining nor fretting, trusting that the boat will come in its own time and that waiting is itself part of the journey.
At the well he waits for the boat, in no hurry, for the boat knows when to come.
well, boat, waiting
I've opened my little stall in the market and the first month has been very slow, but my father tells me trust is built one customer at a time.
market, slow trust
In the market's rush, the quiet one waits; and what is his comes to him unhurried.
doha: be patient in the market
Compose a doha about a vendor in the market who is content to wait for his customers without chasing them, believing that good things come to those who wait calmly and treat others with kindness.
wait for your time
doha about being calm with life
Write a doha about the way patience is the strongest form of faith, for the one who waits without anger or complaint trusts that life will bring what is right when the time is right.
Calm waiting is faith that has learned to sit still.
My best friend has been through two years of failed attempts at starting her career and she is still smiling and trying, and I want to say something encouraging.
Compose a doha about a man who slowly learns that he cannot hurry the course of events, that everything in life has its own time, and that the more he struggles to rush it, the longer it takes.
everything in its time
I kept pushing and pushing to get things done faster at work, and I got sick, and the doctor told me bluntly to slow down and let things take their time.
Everything in its own time: that is the law the hurried heart forgets.
doha on letting things take their time
My grandfather has sat in the same corner of the market for forty years waiting for customers, and I never once saw him upset.
doha: sitting patiently in the market
market, patient man
Write a doha about an old man who sits quietly in the market through every slow day, never hurrying or complaining, trusting that life brings to each person at the right time exactly what they need.
Calm in the market's roar he sits, for time has never failed the patient.
My uncle the potter waits for the well to fill before he mixes his clay, never rushing, and says rushing the work only cracks the pots.
doha: potter and well, waiting matters
The potter waits for the well to fill, and the clay waits for the potter, and all things come at last.
potter, well, patience

Compose a doha about a potter who waits calmly for water to fill the well before he works the clay, understanding that all his labour depends on time, and that no hurry can speed up what nature does slowly.
doha: lamp and potter, no rushing
My cousin makes clay lamps and waits days for them to dry properly in the sun, and never rushes, saying hurried lamps always crack.
Write a doha about a potter who patiently dries his clay lamps in the sun, knowing that each stage needs its own time, and that only the work that has been waited for will burn bright and last.
The potter waits for the lamp to dry, the lamp waits for the flame, and so is the wait rewarded.
potter, lamp, patience
I've been learning a new skill and keep making mistakes because I can't wait, and my mother says you can't hurry anything that's worth making.
don't rush
doha about patience, quick one
Haste robs the hour of what it was bringing.
Write a doha about the folly of rushing through life, how the hurried man misses what the patient man receives, and how every good thing comes to us at its own pace if we let it.

Compose a doha about a potter who sells his vessels at the market and never lowers his price or rushes his customers, waiting patiently for the right buyer, trusting that every piece finds its owner at the right time.
doha: potter at the market waiting for buyers
The potter sits among the market stalls in no hurry, for every vessel finds its hand.
My uncle the potter takes his pots to the market every Saturday and waits patiently all day, and says each one will find its buyer in time.
potter, market, patience
potter, slow clay
doha: potter waiting for clay to dry, patience
My grandfather the potter never rushed the drying of his clay, and said that a hurried pot cracks in the fire, just like a hurried life.
Write a doha about a potter who waits patiently for his clay to dry before it is fired, showing that every stage of making needs its own time and that rushing it only ruins the work.
The clay must dry in its own time, and the potter learns the wisdom of waiting.
